scenes.title: One slot. One confirmed booking.
scenes.text: Two patients choose the same appointment. Who gets it? Slot Zero gives one clear confirmation, while helping doctors and patients stay in sync across time zones.

scenes.title: A workspace for each role
scenes.text: Start at the sign-in page. Doctors enter their scheduling workspace. Patients enter their own dashboard to find a doctor and manage appointments.

scenes.title: Create your patient account
scenes.detail: Name, email, password and local time zone
scenes.text: New patients can register with their name, email, a password of at least ten characters, and a supported time zone. Doctor accounts are provisioned separately.

scenes.title: Your hours become availability
scenes.detail: Weekly ranges, split shifts and consultation length
scenes.text: Dr. Meera sets her London time zone, weekly working hours and a thirty-minute consultation length. Split shifts leave room for lunch. Fifteen and sixty-minute appointments are also supported.

scenes.title: Make room for time off
scenes.detail: Unavailable periods are removed from the slot list
scenes.text: She can add a dated blocked period for a break or time off. The scheduler removes these periods from availability and rejects changes that conflict with confirmed appointments.

scenes.title: Find the right doctor
scenes.detail: Filter by name, specialization and availability date
scenes.text: Now Asha signs in from India. She searches by doctor name, specialization, or availability date. Each doctor card shows the consultation length, time zone and available slots.

scenes.title: Choose a date and time
scenes.detail: The date selector follows the doctor's calendar
scenes.text: She opens Dr. Meera's profile and chooses a date on the doctor's calendar. Slots come from working hours, blocked periods and existing bookings, rather than a fixed timetable.

scenes.title: One appointment. Local times.
scenes.text: The same slot appears in both local times. In this example, ten in the morning in London is three thirty in the afternoon in Kolkata, and five in New York.

scenes.title: Book with a final availability check
scenes.text: Asha selects Book and confirms. The server checks the slot again before saving. Her confirmed appointment appears on her dashboard, with reschedule and cancel actions beside it.

scenes.title: The same booking reaches the doctor
scenes.detail: Asha's appointment, shown in London time
scenes.text: On Dr. Meera's daily calendar, the same booking appears with Asha's details and the doctor's local time. Both views represent the same appointment stored in coordinated universal time.

scenes.title: A clear answer for the second patient
scenes.detail: Asha is confirmed. Sam chooses another time.
scenes.text: If Sam submits the same slot after Asha, he receives an unavailable notice. In this shared-database demo, transaction checks and overlap protection keep that slot to one confirmed booking.

scenes.title: Choose a replacement safely
scenes.detail: The current booking stays until the move succeeds
scenes.text: When plans change, Asha opens Reschedule and selects a replacement. The move succeeds only if that time is still available. A failed move keeps her original booking confirmed.

scenes.title: New time saved. Old slot released.
scenes.text: After a successful move, her dashboard shows the new time and the previous slot becomes available again. The activity log records the change.

scenes.title: Cancel while eligible
scenes.detail: At least two hours before the appointment
scenes.text: Cancellation and rescheduling require at least two hours before the appointment starts in this prototype. Cancelling releases the slot, so another patient can book it if it remains eligible.

scenes.title: Keep a record of every change
scenes.text: Both workspaces keep appointment activity. Patients can also change their display time zone. Local times update while the underlying appointment stays the same.

scenes.title: Appointments, in sync.
scenes.text: That's Slot Zero: doctor-controlled availability, patient self-service, and conflict-checked bookings across India, London and New York. Explore the prototype today. This demonstration uses fictional data; reminders and payments are not included.
